issues.failure_explanation:
For $v \in H^s(K)$, the gradient $
abla v$ is in $\mathbf{H}^{s-1}(K)$, so its $s$-th order Sobolev seminorm $|
abla v|_{s, K} = |v|_{s+1, K}$ is in general undefined or unbounded. Furthermore, the proof applies Theorem 3.10 to $ oldsymbol{w} = 
abla v$, but Theorem 3.10 assumes $ oldsymbol{w} \in \mathbf{H}^s(K)$, which would require $v \in H^{s+1}(K)$, violating the hypothesis $v \in H^s(K)$. Under the stated regularity $v \in H^s(K)$, standard finite element interpolation theory gives an $H^1$-seminorm error of order $O(h_K^{s-1} |v|_{s, K})$, not $O(h_K^s |
abla v|_{s, K})$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $v \in H^{s+1}(K)$ with $1/2 < s \le m$ so that $\nabla v \in \mathbf{H}^s(K)$ legitimately feeds into Theorem 3.10, or alternatively replace the upper bound with $h_K^{s-1} |v|_{s, K}$ for $v \in H^s(K)$ with $3/2 < s \le m+1$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.11 is ill-defined and false as stated for general $v \in H^s(K)$, because the right-hand side is unbounded and the convergence exponent in $h_K$ is overstated by 1 relative to the assumed Sobolev regularity.
issues.title: Sobolev regularity and rate mismatch in serendipity node interpolation theorem
issues.why_classification: The mismatch is a local index shift between scalar functions and their vector gradients that can be resolved either by assuming $v \in H^{s+1}(K)$ or by adjusting the convergence exponent to $h_K^{s-1}$ using standard virtual element interpolation techniques without altering other results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\) monotonically increases with \(l\), it must converges as \(l\rightarrow\infty\). Denote the limit by \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\). By the density of polynomials, \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|=\left\|\boldsymbol{\psi}^\infty_{i}\right\|\). Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some \(l\) making \(\mathbf{M}^l\) full row rank.

we expect that in most cases, the lowest order \(l\) such that the demensionality of the projected space is greater than that of the kernel space, is sufficient to make the projection stable... The minimum \(l\) such that
  \(\mathrm{dim}\left(\nabla \mathbb{P}_{l+1}\right)-\mathrm{dim}\left(\nabla \mathbb{P}_{m+1}\right)\geq N_{S}-N_{P}\)
  is most likely enough.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 3.12 contains multiple fatal mathematical failures: (1) As $l$ increases, the space $\mathbf{V}_l^{\mathrm{S}}$ and its Lagrange basis functions $\boldsymbol{\psi}_i^l$ vary with $l$; the proof claims convergence to a limit object $\boldsymbol{\psi}_i^\infty$, which is never defined and has no established existence in $L^2(K)$. (2) The deduction that 'Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some $l$ making $\mathbf{M}^l$ full row rank' is a non sequitur; linear independence of basis functions in $\mathbf{V}_l^{\mathrm{S}}$ does not imply that their projections onto a polynomial subspace $\mathbb{P}_l^3$ are linearly independent (which is precisely what full row rank of $\mathbf{M}^l$ asserts). (3) The subsequent discussion explicitly concedes that whether any finite $l$ yields stability is only an unproved heuristic expectation ('is most likely enough').
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide an explicit, proven construction or bound showing that the restriction of the $L^2$-projection $\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_l$ to $\mathbf{V}_l^{\mathrm{S}}$ is injective and uniformly bounded from below by a positive constant independent of $h$ for some computable order $l$.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of a computable, stable polynomial projection $\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_l$ without stabilization is not established. Consequently, the equivalent discrete bilinear forms $a_h[\boldsymbol{u}_h, \boldsymbol{v}_h] := a_h(\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_l \boldsymbol{u}_h, \bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_l \boldsymbol{v}_h)$ (Definition 3.13) cannot be guaranteed to be coercive or stable, defeating the main claim of the paper.
issues.title: Unsubstantiated proof and invalid inference for existence of stable polynomial projection
issues.why_classification: The existence of a stable polynomial projection is the foundational theorem justifying the stabilization-free VEM formulation in the paper. Because the proof relies on undefined limits and invalid circular inferences, and no complete resolution exists within the source, a fundamentally new proof architecture is required.
